_comment: 英文覆盖层：按索引对齐 foods/scenes/unis 的中文条目（本文件数组顺序必须与 zh 文件一致）。覆盖 desc/history 叙述字段；名称用各条目已有的 en 字段。
history: Changsha has 3,000 years of history — the 'home of Qu Yuan and Jia Yi', a famous Chu-Han city. The Lady Xinzhui and the gauze dress from Mawangdui amazed the world. At Yuelu Academy, Zhu Xi once lectured; on Orange Isle young Mao Zedong wrote his ambitions. Today Changsha is famous for Hunan TV, milk tea and nightlife — a UNESCO City of Media Arts.
importance: Capital of Hunan · UNESCO City of Media Arts · Trendy internet-famous city
foods: Stinky tofu — smells odd, tastes great; the Fire Palace version is the most authentic.
China's first milk tea with cream-cheese foam — people queue three hours for it.
Sweet sticky rice cakes fried in sugar syrup — a street sweet.
Spicy crayfish — the king of Changsha late-night snacks.
Hunan classic: big fish head steamed with red chopped chili, fresh and hot.
Rice noodles with toppings — 'suo fen' is the Changsha morning ritual.
Spicy crab full of roe — a night-market hit.
Crispy baked bun with preserved-mustard pork filling.
scenes: Long island in the Xiang River with the young Mao Zedong sculpture.
A thousand-year academy — 'Chu has talent, and here it flourishes'.
The Han tomb of Mawangdui and its silk gauze dress.
Thousand-year old street with Jia Yi's former home and a food corridor.
Famous tower on the old city wall — the origin point of Changsha.
Theme park of miniature world wonders.
Poet Du Fu's memorial tower by the Xiang River — best fireworks viewpoint.
Ancient town cluster with stone-paved streets and old shops.
